claims.what: Tier 1 changes only how products and sums are computed, with the serialized weights byte-identical
Tier 1 changed decisions near the threshold, and which ones depended on the GPU and its software stack, but no verdict under the prespecified, unweighted tests
Tier 2 (BF16 compute, FP8 and 8-bit weights) changed more decisions and some diagnostic verdicts, but no four-fifths verdict
three tabular model families and two open-weight language models (4B and 24B parameters) on four public tasks, on CPUs and GPUs from NVIDIA, AMD and Apple
serving the 24B model with vLLM FP8 selected 54% of people rather than 45%

that FP8 configuration passed an employment-status audit by sex that its strict FP32 reference failed, with the demographic-parity gap falling from 0.0567 to 0.0417 and the equalized-odds gap from 0.0515 to 0.0394, against a diagnostic tolerance of 0.05
at the reference's selection count FP8 failed demographic parity, and no reading gave its equalized-odds change a paired interval excluding zero
at the frozen thresholds every pass-fail verdict a configuration changed had a sampling interval containing its criterion
an audit stability protocol in which the auditor declares contracts, groups, weights and tests before scoring and records each verdict's range over them apart from its sampling uncertainty
